subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw permit timeout-driven concurrent same-session `maintain()` calls for existing context-engine plugins, or should lane release require a new engine opt-in capability with cancellation or concurrency semantics?
rationale: The implementation deliberately changes a public plugin callback’s ordering guarantee, and neither host fencing nor documentation can make third-party plugin-private state safe without maintainers choosing the supported compatibility contract.

options.title: Add an opt-in engine capability
options.body: Preserve serialized behavior for existing engines and release a timed-out lane only when an engine explicitly advertises compatible cancellation or re-entrant maintenance semantics.

options.title: Accept the documented contract change
options.body: Keep the current operator opt-in setting and make concurrent maintenance a required responsibility of every installed context-engine plugin.

options.title: Pause this timeout path
options.body: Retain the stalled-warning backoff separately and defer timeout release until the plugin SDK contract is designed and approved.

recommendation.title: Add an opt-in engine capability
recommendation.body: Preserve serialized behavior for existing engines and release a timed-out lane only when an engine explicitly advertises compatible cancellation or re-entrant maintenance semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice sets the repository-wide public plugin compatibility policy.
